title: Electric charge and field idea
text: Electric charge comes in two kinds, positive and negative. Like charges repel; opposite charges attract. The electric field at a point is the force per unit positive test charge at that point. Field lines leave positive charge and enter negative charge. Closer spacing means a stronger field.

title: Single point charge field
text: A lone positive point charge has field lines radiating outward in all directions. A lone negative charge has lines radiating inward. Magnitude falls with distance (Coulomb 1/r² in space). On a 2D board, draw radial arrows or lines around one charge symbol.

title: Electric dipole field
text: An electric dipole is equal and opposite charges separated by a small distance. Field lines leave the positive charge and curve into the negative charge. Along the axis the fields partly add; on the perpendicular bisector they partly cancel. Do not draw closed loops for electrostatic E fields in empty space.

title: Coulomb's law
text: Coulomb's law: the magnitude of the force between two point charges is k|q1 q2|/r², along the line joining them. Direction: repulsion if same sign, attraction if opposite. k is Coulomb's constant. Force on each charge is equal and opposite (Newton's third law).

title: Electric potential vs field
text: Electric potential V is electric potential energy per unit charge. The field points from high potential toward low potential for a positive test charge. Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to field lines. Moving along an equipotential does no work. Potential is a scalar; field is a vector.

title: Conductors in electrostatics
text: In electrostatic equilibrium, the electric field inside a conducting material is zero. Excess charge resides on the outer surface. The conductor is an equipotential. Near a sharp point, surface charge density and field outside are larger. Induced charges rearrange when an external charge approaches.

title: Parallel-plate capacitor
text: An ideal parallel-plate capacitor has equal and opposite charge on two plates. Between the plates the field is approximately uniform and perpendicular to the plates; outside it is nearly zero. Capacitance C = Q/V. Energy stored is (1/2)CV². Adding a dielectric increases C for fixed plate geometry.

title: Charged sheet and wire
text: An infinite charged sheet has a roughly uniform field perpendicular to the sheet on each side. A long charged wire has radial field in the plane perpendicular to the wire, falling like 1/r. Use symmetry (Gauss's law ideas) to argue direction before writing formulas.

title: Superposition of fields
text: Electric fields from several sources add as vectors at each point (superposition). Draw each contribution, then tip-to-tail or components. Cancelling components explain null points between like charges or on a dipole's midplane in the right places.

title: Image charge intuition
text: A point charge near a grounded conducting plane induces opposite surface charge. Outside the conductor, the field matches a simpler 'image' charge behind the plane. Inside the conductor the field stays zero. Use this only as an intuition bridge for high school — mention the image is a calculation trick, not a real charge behind the wall.
